No agent computes, compares or pastes a hash or a file body: the return channel HTML-escapes `<`, `>` and `&`, so a body cannot cross it byte-for-byte, while 64 hex characters can. On each subagent return — **after** obligation 5's run-grain verify and **before** the token is reconciled or any outcome recorded — the dispatcher pipes the returned line (or `null`) into `faff evidence verify-return --run-dir <run_dir> --issue <issue>`, which is read-only (it re-hashes `ac-checklist.json` / `review-verdict.json` / `human-only-acs.json` to the same leaf sha256 `faff integrity-digest hash` reports, and writes nothing), and branches on its exit code: **0** (`agree`) → if the printed `evidence_persisted` is non-null, append it to the ledger **through obligation 5's mandatory re-baseline write sequence** (the ledger is a bracketed member); the per-issue files are never rewritten, and a legitimately absent file (a pre-worktree skip, a `retry-later` that wrote no `review-verdict.json`, an early park/errored) neither parks nor persists. **1** → unit-scoped park with cause = the printed `park_cause` (`evidence-return mismatch — <issue>/<file> (<presence disagreement|returned copy ≠ on-disk copy|on-disk copy is not a regular file>)`, `evidence-return missing — <issue>/<file> (no digest returned for a file on disk)`, or `evidence-return malformed — <issue>/EvidenceReturn (malformed return)`), `faff-parked` + comment, bucket `parked`; for verdict `mismatch` append each string in the printed `tampered_paths` to the `integrity_tampered` array (none for a no-claim-only mismatch), and for verdict `malformed` append nothing, since a transport or lane fault is not evidence that a file changed. **2** (usage, path rejected, hasher unavailable) → unit-scoped park with cause `evidence-return verification unavailable — <stderr first line>` and no `integrity_tampered` entry. The dispatcher keeps nothing from the return past this check; obligation 7's pre-merge re-verify reads the ledger entry instead. Every park here is **unit-scoped**: a per-issue evidence mismatch parks only that unit and never halts-and-drains a wave (obligation 5's run-grain chain guards the shared substrate, and its own tamper response cannot stop in-flight merges either, so escalating buys little while over-scoping is a denial-of-service amplifier). **Honest scope:** this adds tamper-between-write-and-return detection ahead of consumption; it does **not** make the files' *content* independent of the authoring lane — a lane that authors the on-disk copy and returns its digest passes, so content-independence stays the code-blind holdout's job (obligation 4), never claimed here. For `human-only-acs.json` the digest covers the run-dir copy the lane minted, while merge-gate reads the committed anchored copy against the events stamp, so the digest is a tamper witness over the mint's source and not the bytes the floor consumes. **Post-relocation (slice 2):** the lane keeps its own AC/review writes because the Step-9b anchor reads them pre-return, and the dispatcher-verified files are what the dispatcher-run merge consumes (obligation 7). This is **detection ahead of consumption; it never changes obligation 4's merge floor.** Occupants carry only their own placement prose (where in their return-handling the check runs) and refer back here — never restate it. **Interactive top-level graft has no dispatch cut above it and is out of scope (the carve-out); this obligation binds only a dispatched build lane.**

7. **Run the merge above the cut — the dispatcher is the merge locus (relocation slice 2; dispatched lane only).** Slice 1 (obligation 6) moved verification of the merge-consumed evidence to the dispatcher; this slice moves the *merge itself* there, so the dispatcher-verified `ac-checklist.json` / `review-verdict.json` are the files the merge actually consumes (resolving slice 1's transitional in-lane-merge coupling — the dispatcher re-verifies them immediately before consuming them, on the trusted side). A dispatched build lane now ends at **PR-ready** — gates green, PR opened, evidence returned — and returns outcome `pr-ready`, performing **no** merge (no ship handoff, no `merge-gate`, no `merge-record.json`, no post-merge tail); one coherent invariant holds with obligation 6: **a lane returns `EvidenceReturn` ⟺ there is a dispatch cut ⟺ that lane does not merge; the dispatcher merges.** **Custody wiring — the dispatched-lane detective-custody producer that arms the dormant custody merge gate.** Once at pass start, **before the first dispatch**, the dispatcher emits the build-lane boundary — `faff lane-boundary emit --run-dir <run_dir> --lane build` — so the run reads `dispatched` (`laneBoundaryDispatchState`) and `evaluateCustody` becomes **required** for every merge in the run dir, while a `build` lane can never arm the evaluator cage (`laneBoundaryPromisesCage` stays keyed on `lane === "evaluator"`, so the widened vocabulary is dispatch-only, never a cage promise). A non-zero emit **parks the pass before any dispatch** — a half-wired run (boundary present, no threaded verdict) would refuse every merge. This is genuine **detective** custody (a trusted dispatcher verifying an *untrusted* lane's forge surface), never the interactive `--local` self-consistency stamp, and the verdict is never fed through `FAFF_INTEGRITY_BOUNDARY` (the two-basis discipline).
